source.title: A Mini-Block Natural Gradient Method for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Achraf Bahamou; D. Goldfarb; Yi Ren

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present, with duplicated and partially garbled supplementary text; the main CNN results and optimizer comparison table are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification performance across optimizers using CNNs and validation accuracy, testing the optimizer-generalization comparison with a different method and setting.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports training-loss, timing, and optimizer-direction comparisons; those do not measure the optimizer-related held-out performance in V4. The reported CNN accuracy table gives averages across five runs, while its standard deviations appear only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimization with momentum SGD using held-out classification accuracy, the method and measure relevant to V4. Its CNN implementations use AdamW-style and SGDW-style decoupled weight decay, with learning rate and weight decay tuned.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's CNN summary is accurate: the authors conclude that MBF has comparable and sometimes better generalization performance than the comparison methods. Their broader conclusion also covers optimization performance and computational efficiency; it does not assert that Adam uniformly generalizes worse than SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a new mini-block Fisher optimizer against Adam and SGD-m on three CNN dataset-model pairs; all CNN methods use weight decay, with learning rate and weight decay selected by grid search.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset-model pair changes the Adam versus SGD-m validation-accuracy ordering; CIFAR-10/ResNet32 favors Adam slightly, while CIFAR-100/VGG16 and SVHN/VGG11 favor SGD-m.

fits_no_version.finding: Autoencoder experiments compare reconstruction training losses and validation errors rather than classification or language performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects reconstruction optimization and held-out reconstruction performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Direction cosine similarities and inverse-Fisher heatmaps assess preconditioner approximations, without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mini-block Fisher approximations retain useful structure and approximate full-block update directions.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (as stated in supplied metadata); paper text also labels the manuscript under review.
record.problems: The comparison covers only three CNN dataset-model pairs and reports validation accuracy rather than a direct training-test error gap. The table gives five-run averages, but numeric uncertainty is not tabulated; standard-deviation ranges are shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly measuring the Adam-versus-SGD-m validation-performance comparison were omitted. Other optimizer rows in Table 8 concern MBF, KFAC, and Shampoo, which are not the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison named by V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected classification comparisons and learned local connectivity.

Language benchmarks; learning-rate-only tuning without weight-decay tuning; a controlled comparison establishing that broader tuning or decoupling weight decay removes a previous deficit; switching from Adam to SGD. Figure 17 includes training curves, but the supplied text does not permit determining whether Adam achieves equal or better training performance in each CNN comparison.
Batch-size sweeps, fixed-epoch large-batch penalties, and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout ablations and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Table 8 values are five-run averages. Standard deviations are depicted graphically but cannot be quantified from the supplied text. The nominal test sets serve as validation sets for hyperparameter selection, so these are tuned held-out accuracies rather than results on a separate untouched test set. The six rows represent three paired comparisons. No controlled coupled-versus-decoupled weight-decay ablation establishes a causal recovery effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks; decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD; broader tuning beyond the reported learning-rate and weight-decay grids; optimizer comparisons on other datasets.
Large-batch generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to training-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100/VGG16; 200 epochs, batch size 128, augmentation, tuned learning rate and decoupled weight decay
relationships.reason: R3–R4 report Adam accuracy of 72.95% versus SGD-m at 73.99%, showing an adaptive-optimizer deficit under this recipe.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam accuracy than momentum SGD after learning-rate and decoupled-weight-decay tuning remains unverified.

relationships.condition: SVHN/VGG11; 200 epochs with tuned learning rate and decoupled weight decay
relationships.reason: R5–R6 show only a small Adam deficit: 96.34% versus 96.63%; numerical uncertainty and significance are not supplied.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly trailed momentum SGD slightly, but the comparison remains unverified and uncertainty was unavailable.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10/ResNet32; 200 epochs with tuned learning rate and decoupled weight decay
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show a small reversal, with Adam at 93.34% versus SGD-m at 93.23%, consistent with V4's recipe-dependent qualification.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly slightly exceeded momentum SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.
